desc:
The binary reflected Gray code sequence is g(0), g(1), g(2), ... where g(i) = i XOR (i >> 1). It starts 0, 1, 3, 2, 6, 7, 5, 4, 12, ...: consecutive values differ in exactly one bit, and every non-negative integer appears exactly once. The Gray position of a number x is the index i with g(i) = x, so 3 has position 2 and 4 has position 7.

Return nums sorted by Gray position in ascending order (the order in which the numbers appear in the Gray code sequence).

Example: nums = [4, 2, 7, 0] has positions 7, 3, 5, 0, so the answer is [0, 2, 7, 4].
hints: You cannot generate the sequence up to 109. You need the position of x directly, which means inverting g(i) = i XOR (i >> 1).
Look at the bits from the top. The top bit of i equals the top bit of x, and every next bit of i is the previous bit of i XOR the matching bit of x.
That means bit k of i is the XOR of all bits of x at positions k and above. Compute i = x ^ (x >> 1) ^ (x >> 2) ^ ... and sort by it.
editorial: From x = i ^ (i >> 1) we get, for every bit k, x_k = i_k XOR i_(k+1). Solving from the top bit downward gives i_k = x_k XOR i_(k+1), so i_k is the XOR (parity) of the bits of x at positions k, k+1, and so on. All of these bits at once equal x ^ (x >> 1) ^ (x >> 2) ^ ..., which a simple loop computes in at most 30 steps.
Because Gray code is a bijection, different numbers have different positions, so sorting by position is a strict total order. Sort in O(n log n) time with O(n) space for the keys.
